title: Filter nodes with WHERE
summary: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern.
introduction: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern. Your task: Change the minimum to 30.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for filter nodes with where

blocks.text: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern. It can filter a numeric property such as page count.
Use Neo4j 5+ locally with Neo4j Browser or another Cypher editor. These queries use fictional cma-prefixed ids. Cypher is not SQL and does not run in this site's SQL playground.

blocks.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH "cma-" AND b.pages>=50 RETURN b.title,b.pages;
blocks.title: Filter nodes with WHERE

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.
`MATCH` finds the described graph pattern. Labels and arrow direction narrow the connections being followed.

blocks.text: The sample 60-page Moon Trip matches, while the 40-page Garden Days does not.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use the practice-id prefix so this exercise does not accidentally include unrelated graph data.
